rule.description: In a single Go package, a data clump is a contiguous group of three or more declared parameters, identified by identical types in the same order, that recurs across three or more distinct function or method signatures. Receivers are excluded (a receiver is the owning instance, not a value the caller hands over), _test.go files are excluded, and signatures whose parameter types cannot be resolved are skipped rather than silently passed. Occurrences nested inside a longer qualifying run of the same signature are subsumed by the longer run.
rule.backend_binding: golang.org/x/tools v0.13.0 go/analysis analyzer 'paramclump' driven through singlechecker.Main; type identity via types.TypeString(t, types.RelativeTo(pass.Pkg)); exit code 0 = no diagnostics, 3 = diagnostics reported, 1 = analysis failed.

checks.description: A* search bookkeeping state (open priority queue, closed set, node-to-wrapper registry) is threaded as three separate parameters through every step of the search loop in package astar instead of being owned by one abstraction.
checks.detected_relation: The ordered parameter group [*priorityqueues.PriorityQueue[*wrapper], *hashsets.HashSet[*wrapper], map[Node]*wrapper] recurs as a contiguous run in 3 distinct signatures of package astar: search, updateVertex, and clearSearch all receive the same three bookkeeping values side by side.
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: These three values are the per-search bookkeeping of the A* engine: they are created together in one place, mutated together by every step, and cleared together between searches. Carrying them as separate arguments at every step is a textbook data clump - the group itself is the missing search-state abstraction, while the genuine per-call inputs (start and goal nodes, the current and neighbor wrappers) are deliberately left outside the recurring run.

matches.evidence: func search(start Node, goal Node, openPQ *priorityqueues.PriorityQueue[*wrapper], closedSet *hashsets.HashSet[*wrapper], nodeWrapperMap map[Node]*wrapper) []Node (a_star.go:67) - repeats the three bookkeeping parameters immediately after the two genuine per-call nodes.
matches.measurement: contiguous parameter run of 3 identical types recurring in 3 distinct signatures of package astar

matches.evidence: func updateVertex(currentWrapper *wrapper, neighborWrapper *wrapper, goalWrapper *wrapper, openPQ *priorityqueues.PriorityQueue[*wrapper], closedSet *hashsets.HashSet[*wrapper], nodeWrapperMap map[Node]*wrapper) (a_star.go:114) - extends the same run with three leading per-call wrappers, so the recurring group is a middle segment of a longer signature.
matches.measurement: contiguous parameter run of 3 identical types recurring in 3 distinct signatures of package astar

matches.evidence: func clearSearch(openPQ *priorityqueues.PriorityQueue[*wrapper], closedSet *hashsets.HashSet[*wrapper], nodeWrapperMap map[Node]*wrapper) (a_star.go:135) - resets exactly the same three values and nothing else, the clearest signal that they form one lifecycle unit.
matches.measurement: contiguous parameter run of 3 identical types recurring in 3 distinct signatures of package astar

checks.description: Grid navigation and rendering helpers in package grids all re-receive the grid world plus a cell position as separate parameters instead of reaching them through one owner or location abstraction.
checks.detected_relation: The ordered parameter group [*GridWorld, int, int] recurs as a contiguous run in 4 distinct signatures of package grids: drawCell, isBehindObstacles, isOpen, and nodeAt all take world and two integer coordinates side by side.
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: A grid cell is only meaningful relative to the world it lives in, and every one of these helpers re-validates bounds, looks the node up, or paints at (x, y) through the same world-plus-position pair. Passing world, x, and y separately through the traversal step, the obstacle lookup, and the image-export paint loop is the classic missing-owner clump: the world instance is the natural owner and the (i, j) pair is a location, yet both travel as three loose scalars. The genuine per-call other node in isBehindObstacles and the drawing dependencies in drawCell are deliberately left outside the recurring run so the boundary must be read from the domain, not from type repetition alone.

matches.evidence: func drawCell(world *GridWorld, row int, column int, grid *gridder.Gridder, face font.Face) (grid_generator.go:64) - the image-export paint step re-receives world and the cell coordinates as three separate arguments before its rendering dependencies.
matches.measurement: contiguous parameter run of 3 identical types recurring in 4 distinct signatures of package grids

matches.evidence: func isBehindObstacles(world *GridWorld, x int, y int, node *GridNode) bool (grid_node.go:63) - obstacle-shadow test re-receives the world and coordinates of the cell being tested, plus the neighbor as a genuine per-call argument.
matches.measurement: contiguous parameter run of 3 identical types recurring in 4 distinct signatures of package grids

matches.evidence: func isOpen(world *GridWorld, i int, j int) bool (grid_world.go:43) - bound check plus obstacle test repeated as a free function over world and a coordinate pair.
matches.measurement: contiguous parameter run of 3 identical types recurring in 4 distinct signatures of package grids

matches.evidence: func nodeAt(world *GridWorld, i int, j int) *GridNode (grid_world.go:51) - bounds-guarded node lookup with the same world-plus-position trio.
matches.measurement: contiguous parameter run of 3 identical types recurring in 4 distinct signatures of package grids

checks.description: Word-breaker parsing state (input text, dictionary set, memo cache) is handed over as three separate parameters at every level of the recursion in package wordbreakers instead of being owned by one parse abstraction.
checks.detected_relation: The ordered parameter group [string, *hashsets.HashSet[string], map[string]string] recurs as a contiguous run in 3 distinct signatures of package wordbreakers: breakWord, firstKnownWord, and extractWords all receive input, dictionary, and cache side by side.
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The dictionary and memo cache are shared parse state that lives for the duration of one BreakWord or ExtractWords call, yet they are re-threaded piecemeal through the recursion and the memo is keyed by the same input string that also rides along as a separate argument. Parsing state that always travels together is a data clump; note that input is also a genuine per-recursion value that changes at each level, which makes deciding the correct boundary a domain judgment rather than a mechanical grouping.

matches.evidence: func breakWord(input string, dictionary *hashsets.HashSet[string], cache map[string]string) (string, bool) (word_breaker.go:24) - the public BreakWord delegates here, re-threading input and both pieces of shared parse state.
matches.measurement: contiguous parameter run of 3 identical types recurring in 3 distinct signatures of package wordbreakers

matches.evidence: func firstKnownWord(input string, dictionary *hashsets.HashSet[string], cache map[string]string) (string, bool) (word_breaker.go:47) - dictionary-or-memo probe over the same three values, created to demonstrate that the trio keeps recurring as new helpers were extracted.
matches.measurement: contiguous parameter run of 3 identical types recurring in 3 distinct signatures of package wordbreakers

matches.evidence: func extractWords(input string, dictionary *hashsets.HashSet[string], cache map[string]string) []string (word_breaker.go:75) - the recursive extraction walk re-receives the identical parameter group, completing the third recurrence in the package.
matches.measurement: contiguous parameter run of 3 identical types recurring in 3 distinct signatures of package wordbreakers

checks.description: Sliding-window bookkeeping (running sum, window capacity, element queue) is threaded as three separate parameters through the window arithmetic in package movingaverages instead of being owned by one window abstraction.
checks.detected_relation: The ordered parameter group [*int, int, *queues.Queue[int]] recurs as a contiguous run in 3 distinct signatures of package movingaverages: addToWindow, evict, and windowAverage all take sum, windowSize, and queue side by side.
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: sum, windowSize, and queue are the invariant state of the sliding window: appending a number adjusts all three together (enqueue, bump the sum, evict and subtract once the capacity is exceeded), and reading the average consults two of them. The sum even travels as a raw *int pointing into the owning struct, showing the group was chopped out of an existing owner. Threading a pointer plus a capacity plus a container as three arguments at every step is the data clump this task targets; windowSize being unused by windowAverage at the end of the run marks the boundary as something the maintainer must reason about rather than group mechanically.

matches.evidence: func addToWindow(sum *int, windowSize int, queue *queues.Queue[int], number int) (moving_averages.go:35) - the public Add delegates here with (&ma.sum, ma.windowSize, ma.queue), re-threading the window state plus the genuine per-call number.
matches.measurement: contiguous parameter run of 3 identical types recurring in 3 distinct signatures of package movingaverages

matches.evidence: func evict(sum *int, windowSize int, queue *queues.Queue[int]) (moving_averages.go:42) - over-capacity eviction consumes exactly the three-value state and nothing else.
matches.measurement: contiguous parameter run of 3 identical types recurring in 3 distinct signatures of package movingaverages

matches.evidence: func windowAverage(sum *int, windowSize int, queue *queues.Queue[int]) float64 (moving_averages.go:52) - the average read receives all three values although it only needs two, recording that the group is copied around wholesale.
matches.measurement: contiguous parameter run of 3 identical types recurring in 3 distinct signatures of package movingaverages
